=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py: lines 511-519 (lookups_needed), 584-599 (decide lookup merge), 652-657 (new _is_active guard) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new `_is_active(view, now)` guard is bypassed for page-listed checkers because `lookups_needed()` (line 518: `if checker in on_page or checker in bound: continue`) skips `get_session` for any checker already present on the session page, and `decide()` (lines 588-590: `if checker in by_id: continue`) ignores any lookup result that happens to arrive for an id already in `by_id`.
  WHY: For page-listed checkers `view` is the stale page record, so a checker that re-armed after the session page was read and whose page `updated_at` is outside the 90-minute window will be listed for restart, producing a duplicate check-in / duplicate stage; the two new tests do not exercise that page-listed-with-stale-snapshot case.

- Requirement: "keep a checker that itself ran in the last 90 minutes" (PR title and description). The PR description explicitly identifies the live failure mode — a checker that "re-armed or started its next stage after the trigger and session pages were read" — and the new tests on lines 291-300 are framed as the regression coverage for that class of bug. The README (lines 1293-1299), agents.md (lines 295-298), and changelog fragment (line 18) all describe the behaviour as "the checker's own last turn counts" / "ran in the last 90 minutes is kept" without any page-staleness qualifier.
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_checker_restart.py lines 511-531 (lookups_needed skip rule) plus the merge at lines 588-599, so that a page-listed checker whose page snapshot is stale can still be kept by the guard; and a regression test in tests/test_claude_checker_restart.py that puts a checker on the page with `updated_at` outside the 90-minute window and exercises the page-listed path (not the looked-up path used by `test_condition_4_a_looked_up_checker_that_handed_off_after_the_page_is_kept`).
  Evidence of absence: The new `_is_active(view, now)` check at line 652 evaluates `view["updated_at"]` from `by_id`, which is populated from `state["sessions"]` at line 585. For page-listed checkers, `lookups_needed()` line 518 short-circuits before `get_session` is called, and `decide()` lines 588-590 discard any lookup result whose id is already in `by_id`. The two on-page new tests (lines 291-300) put `updated_at = MINUTES_AGO` (kept) or `updated_at = 91 minutes ago` (restarted); no test puts a checker on the page with `updated_at` outside the window while passing a fresher signal that should override the stale page record. README line 1296, agents.md line 297, and changelog.d/4910-restart-dead-checkers.md line 18 all describe the behaviour in absolute terms ("the checker's own last turn counts", "ran in the last 90 minutes is kept"), not in terms of the page-snapshot limitation the implementation actually leaves for page-listed checkers.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- lines 652-658 (new `_is_active(view, now)` check) interacting with `lookups_needed()` at line 518 and `decide()` at line 589 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: For a checker that is already on the session page, `view` at line 613 is the page snapshot, not a fresh `get_session` result; `lookups_needed()` (line 518: `if checker in on_page or checker in bound: continue`) skips page-listed checkers, and `decide()` (line 589) ignores any lookup result that arrives for them, so `_is_active(view, now)` at line 652 evaluates the stale page `updated_at`.
  WHY: A page-listed checker whose page `updated_at` is older than 90 minutes but that re-armed or started a stage in the seconds between the page read and `decide()` is still listed for restart, creating the duplicate check-in/stage the PR aims to prevent.

- Requirement: PR title / description: "keep a checker that itself ran in the last 90 minutes" — closes the duplicate check-in / duplicate stage window for a checker that re-armed or started its next stage after the trigger and session pages were read.

For a page-listed checker whose page `updated_at` is older than 90 minutes but that re-armed after the page was read, `lookups_needed()` skips the `get_session` refresh (line 518) and `decide()` ignores any lookup result (line 589), so the stale snapshot is evaluated and the checker is restarted — the duplicate the requirement says is prevented. No test exercises that on-page-stale case. The docs (README, agents.md, changelog) describe the behavior without the page-staleness qualifier, overstating the coverage that option A actually delivers.
